claims.text: The target material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The target HfNbTaTiZr alloy is single-phase BCC.
The modeled alloy is defect-free and chemically homogeneous.
Chemical short-range order affects the stiffness of HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order produces associated local lattice distortions.
Variations in local stoichiometry induce changes in elastic moduli.
Local chemical order and its lattice distortions modify phonon-scattering paths and rates.
Separately resolving these local effects from electronic transport enables accurate calculation of lattice thermal conductivity.
Earlier Debye-based or simplified analytical approaches fail to capture the relevant effects of local chemical ordering.
Previous Debye-based or transport-conflating estimates typically have errors of 20–30% or more.
The new approach will predict lattice thermal conductivity within 10% of experiment from 300 to 1200 K.
Below 200 K, the model will predict a distinct temperature dependence representing a pure phonon contribution decoupled from electronic transport.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions are comparable in HfNbTaTiZr.
The claimed 300–1200 K accuracy applies to high-purity samples containing less than 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model's applicability is limited to single-phase, defect-free BCC HfNbTaTiZr.
Secondary phases and impurities introduce additional scattering that can reduce model accuracy.
The high-temperature regime from 300 to 1200 K is dominated by lattice heat conduction.
Laser-flash analysis corrected using electronic-transport information can independently determine lattice thermal conductivity.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can isolate the phonon contribution in these specimens.
A deviation greater than 10% over 300–1200 K or absence of the predicted association between local chemical order and phonon scattering would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated domain is defect-free material, yet uncertainty in the prediction is attributed to local dislocation behavior; dislocations are defects and therefore fall outside the declared material state unless the term 'defect-free' is narrowed.

The conditions emphasize separating lattice and electronic contributions, including their comparability below 200 K, while the experimental design asserts without qualification that lattice conduction dominates at 300–1200 K. That dominance is neither established nor required if electronic subtraction is performed.
